# AGENTS.md

Instructions for the opencode agent working in this repository.

## What this repository is

- `prompts/triage.md` is the instruction used when the agent answers a newly
  opened issue automatically.
- `.github/workflows/` contains the workflows that drive this agent and the
  `release.yml` workflow that publishes a build.
- `.github/scripts/` contains the tooling the agent uses:
  - `run-opencode-fallback.sh` runs the agent with model fallback and a test gate.
  - `publish-release.sh` builds something and publishes it as a release asset.
  - `gh-account.sh` does the account level operations.
  - `tests/run-opencode-fallback.test.sh` runs the fallback wrapper against
    stubbed `opencode` and `npm` binaries; no provider key or network needed.

There is no binary in the source tree any more.  The build output of
opencode v2.0.22 lives in the release `v2.0.22` of this repository.

## The rule about build output

**Build output is never committed to the source tree.  Every build ends in a
GitHub Release and the binary is an asset of that release.**

Use the script, it builds in a scratch directory, it never touches the
checkout and it never commits anything:

```bash
.github/scripts/publish-release.sh \
    --repo mdmuntakim/ld --clone https://github.com/mdmuntakim/ld --branch main \
    --build "make" --artifact bin/ld \
    --tag v0.1.0 --name "ld 0.1.0" --notes "what the release contains"
```

The script prints the URL of the release.  That URL is the deliverable, it
belongs in the answer to the issue.

The same thing can be done from the Actions tab: **Actions → release → Run
workflow**.

## Projects get their own repository

`mdmuntakim/opencode` is the control repository for the agent.  A project that an
issue asks for (an app, a module, a daemon, a binary) lives in its **own**
repository under `mdmuntakim/`, never in this one and never as a release here.

1. Create the repository (public, like the other project repositories):

   ```bash
   .github/scripts/gh-account.sh repo-create sipolicy --public \
       --description "Kernel-assisted command policy for Android"
   ```

2. Commit the complete source to the new repository's `main` and push it.
   The project's build script, sources, tests and CI belong there too.
3. Build and test in the new repository.  For a native or Magisk project the
   CI must build and exercise every supported ABI; the release notes must
   list the ABI test matrix and its result.
4. Publish the release there with both the build output and the source:

   ```bash
   .github/scripts/publish-release.sh \
       --repo mdmuntakim/sipolicy --clone https://github.com/mdmuntakim/sipolicy \
       --branch main --build "bash build.sh" \
       --artifact sipolicy/dist/sipolicy-0.109.zip \
       --source-archive \
       --tag sipolicy-0.109 --name "sipolicy 0.109" --notes "what changed"
   ```

`--source-archive` adds `<project>-<tag>-source.tar.gz` to the release.  Every
project release includes it, together with the checksums the script writes.

## Long builds: never reach GitHub's 6 hour limit

A job must never run longer than **350 minutes**.  For a build that can take
longer, use the checkpointed continuation workflow in `mdmuntakim/game-forge`
(`.github/workflows/build.yml`):

- the job has `timeout-minutes: 350`;
- the build itself is stopped at 19800 s (5h30m);
- sources, import cache and build output are written to a checkpoint artifact;
- the workflow dispatches a new run with `previous_run=<run-id>`;
- the new run restores the checkpoint, cancels the old run, and continues.

Build commands must be resumable (`make`, `ninja`, SCons, Godot import/export).
Never let a job be killed by GitHub at 6h: a killed job loses its workspace and
cannot hand off.

## Access to the other repositories of the owner

The agent runs with a token that has access to **all** repositories of the
`mmunki` account, not only this one.  That means you can:

- read another repository: `gh repo view mdmuntakim/<repo>`, `gh api repos/mdmuntakim/<repo>`
- clone it: `git clone https://github.com/mdmuntakim/<repo>`
- open a pull request against it: `gh pr create --repo mdmuntakim/<repo> ...`
- create a release in it: `gh release create --repo mdmuntakim/<repo> ...`
- create a repository: `.github/scripts/gh-account.sh repo-create NAME --private`

Prefer `gh` for anything that touches the GitHub API, it is already
authenticated through `GH_TOKEN`.

## The account itself

`.github/scripts/gh-account.sh` wraps the account level operations:

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `whoami` | the login, the id, the plan and the scopes of the token in use |
| `scopes` | the scopes of the token in use |
| `profile` | shows the profile |
| `profile bio="..." company="..." hireable=false` | changes the profile (name, e-mail, bio, company, blog, location, twitter) |
| `username` | shows the login |
| `username newname` | explains how to rename the account |
| `emails` | the e-mail addresses of the account |
| `ssh-keys` | the public SSH keys of the account |
| `pat --name NAME [--repo OWNER/NAME] [--out FILE]` | creates a new personal access token |
| `repo-create NAME [--public\|--private] [--description TEXT]` | creates a repository |

Two things have to be known about these operations:

- **The login of the account cannot be changed with an API.**  GitHub only
  allows it in the browser, `username` prints the exact steps.  Everything
  else about the account (display name, e-mail, bio, company, blog, location,
  SSH keys, tokens, repository visibility) is done through the script.
- **Creating a token needs the `OPENCODE_ADMIN_TOKEN` secret.**  A classic
  token cannot create other tokens, only a fine grained token with
  `Administration: write` can.  Without that secret the `pat` command stops
  with a clear message and everything else still works.

A token that the script creates is written to a file with mode 600, it is
never printed into a comment or into a log.  Store it with:

```bash
gh secret set OPENCODE_ADMIN_TOKEN --repo mdmuntakim/opencode < token.txt
```

## Rules

- Write answers as chat messages in Markdown. Do not paste raw JSON, tool-call
  payloads or action logs into issues and pull requests.
- **Never delete source code.**  No file leaves the source tree because the
  agent decided that it looks obsolete.  A file is only removed when the owner
  removes it or when the owner puts the path into
  `.github/source-protection-allow.txt`.  The `protect-source` workflow fails
  every pull request that deletes a file.
- Never rewrite history, never force push, never delete a branch or a tag,
  never delete a release that is already published.
- Never commit a build output, a binary or an archive to the source tree.
  Publish it as a release asset instead.
- Do not commit secrets, tokens or `.env` files.
- Keep changes to the `main` branch minimal and focused; create a branch for
  anything non-trivial.
- The `gh` CLI is authenticated as the repository owner, so `gh` commands that
  write (issue comments, PRs, branches, releases) act as that user.

# opencode

Personal opencode agent. Ask it anything through GitHub Issues.

The agent decides what to answer, investigate or build, and GitHub Actions runs it.

Every answer, investigation and build is triggered from an issue on this repository.

## What is in here

| Path | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `.github/workflows/opencode.yml` | Answers questions asked in issue / PR comments. |
| `.github/workflows/opencode-triage.yml` | Automatically answers newly opened issues. |
| `.github/workflows/release.yml` | Builds something and publishes it as a release. |
| `.github/workflows/protect-source.yml` | Fails pull requests that delete source files. |
| `.github/workflows/scripts-test.yml` | Lints the shell tooling and tests the agent runner. |
| `.github/scripts/publish-release.sh` | Builds an artefact and publishes it as a release asset. |
| `.github/scripts/gh-account.sh` | The account level operations (profile, tokens, repositories). |
| `.github/scripts/run-opencode-fallback.sh` | Runs the agent with model fallback and a test gate. |
| `prompts/triage.md` | The instruction used for automatic issue triage. |
| `AGENTS.md` | Context the agent loads for this repository. |

There is **no binary in the source tree**. Every build ends in a GitHub
Release and the binary is an asset of that release.

A *project* that an issue asks for (an app, a module, a daemon) gets its own
repository under `mdmuntakim/`; this repository is only the control plane. Project
releases are published in the project repository and always include the source
archive (`--source-archive`) next to the build and its checksums.

## How to use it

### Where does the answer appear?

**As a comment on the issue, right below your question.**

When you ask, the agent immediately adds a `👀` reaction to your comment and
posts a short `[Working...]` placeholder comment that links to the run. When
the agent finishes it **edits that same comment** into the final answer, so the
issue ends up with exactly one comment from the agent and no leftover
placeholder. The run log stays available under the
`[github run]` link at the bottom of the answer.

If the agent decides the issue needs a code change, it opens a pull request and
replies with a `Created PR #<n>` comment instead of a prose answer.

### Memory and reply style

Every agent job gets an explicit 8 GiB heap budget
(`NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192`); the hosted runner itself has
16 GiB. Answers are posted as ordinary chat-style Markdown comments, not as
raw JSON or tool-call transcripts.

### Ask a question

Open an issue (or comment on an existing one) and write:

```
/oc what does the release of this repository contain?
```

or

```
/opencode explain how the triage workflow works
```

The agent reads the whole thread, then replies with its answer. If the answer
requires code changes it opens a pull request instead.

### Post-run validation

`run-opencode-fallback.sh` runs `npm test` after a model finishes, but only
when the repository actually has a `test` script in `package.json`. This
control repository has no application code, so its `package.json` maps
`npm test` to the shell regression suite that covers the agent runner; that
gives the gate something real to execute instead of failing with
`ENOENT: no such file or directory, open .../package.json`. A repository
without a manifest (or without a `test` script) is not a failed run: the gate
is skipped and `npm` is never started. The gate reads `GITHUB_WORKSPACE` (the
checkout root) so it does not matter which directory the workflow invokes the
script from, and it is skipped when `npm` is not installed. A failing test
suite is fed back to the model (the last 200 log lines) for up to
`OPENCODE_TEST_RETRIES` attempts.

A stall or a timeout aborts the agent process itself and moves to the next
model. The wrapper no longer streams through `tee`, because `$!` pointed at
`tee` and the timeout left the real agent running in the background.

The runner and its tests also run in CI on every pull request:

```bash
npm test        # the same shell suite, through the package manifest
npm run lint    # shellcheck on the runner and its tests
npm run check   # both
```

### Automatic answers

Every newly opened issue is answered automatically by the triage workflow.
Only the `opened` event is a trigger - if `edited` were included, GitHub would
emit a second event right after creation and every new issue would be
answered twice.

### Manual run

Go to **Actions → opencode-triage → Run workflow** and type your own prompt.

## Releases

Build output is never committed to the source tree. It is always published as
a release asset, and the release URL is what the agent reports back.

The SHA-256 of every published asset is written into the notes of the release,
so a download can be verified against the release it came from.

The releases of this repository:

- https://github.com/mdmuntakim/opencode/releases

Ask for a build and the agent publishes it:

```
/oc build the final ld binary from mdmuntakim/ld and publish it as a release
```

The same can be done from the Actions tab: **Actions → release → Run
workflow**. The build always runs in a scratch copy of the source, so the
checkout is never modified.

### Downloading the .deb

The package is published as a release asset, byte-for-byte as it was built,
so the blob on GitHub has the exact same SHA-1 as the file on the device:

```bash
gh release download v2.0.22 --repo mdmuntakim/opencode \
  --pattern 'opencode_2.0.22_aarch64.deb'
```

Verify it after downloading:

```bash
sha256sum opencode_2.0.22_aarch64.deb
# 629b6819e40418b96a8dedfc15f8b6cac8f5e4b54682d9f4194c59b68aa95829
```

## Reach of the agent

The agent authenticates with a token that has access to **every repository of
the `mdmuntakim` account**, so it can read and modify any of them, not just this
one. You can ask it to work on another repository:

```
/oc fix the failing build in mdmuntakim/su and open a PR there
```

It can also work on the account itself - the profile, the repositories, the
releases and the tokens. `.github/scripts/gh-account.sh` is the interface:

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `whoami`, `scopes` | the login, the id and the scopes of the token in use |
| `profile`, `profile bio="..." company="..."` | shows and changes the profile |
| `username` | shows the login and explains how to rename the account |
| `emails`, `ssh-keys` | the e-mail addresses and the SSH keys of the account |
| `pat --name NAME [--repo OWNER/NAME]` | creates a new personal access token |
| `repo-create NAME [--public\|--private]` | creates a repository |

Two limits are worth knowing:

- **The login of the account cannot be changed with an API.** GitHub only
  allows it in the browser, `username` prints the exact steps.
- **Creating a token needs the `OPENCODE_ADMIN_TOKEN` secret**, a fine grained
  token with `Administration: write`. A classic token cannot create other
  tokens. Without that secret the `pat` command stops with a clear message
  and everything else still works.

## Setup details

- **Model** – the runner uses free models only, in this fallback chain:
  `opencode/glm-5.3-flash-free opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free
  opencode/flint-40b-free opencode/beam-free
  opencode/mimo-v2.6-flash-free`.  The first entry is used for the session and
  the rest back it up when a model stalls, times out or hits a free tier limit,
  so the job keeps running on free capacity as long as one entry holds. No
  provider API key is required. To use a keyed model, add an `OPENCODE_API_KEY`
  secret and set the repository variable `OPENCODE_MODELS` to a chain that
  lists the keyed models first, for example
  `opencode-go/glm-5.3-flash opencode-go/kimi-k2.7-code`. Free models are rotated
  by the provider, so if a run fails with `Model not found` or
  `Free usage limit reached`, pick a working model and update the
  `OPENCODE_MODELS` variable. Google/Gemini is not used, even when a
  `GOOGLE_API_KEY` or `GEMINI_API_KEY` secret exists.
- **Permissions** – a headless runner has nobody to approve a prompt.
  `external_directory` and `doom_loop` default to `"ask"`, so the agent used
  to wait forever and the job was cancelled at GitHub's 6 hour limit. The
  repository therefore has an `opencode.json` with `"permission": "allow"`,
  and both workflows export `{"*":"allow"}` in `OPENCODE_PERMISSION` so every
  permission is granted automatically, also when the agent works in a scratch
  directory. The agent jobs also have `timeout-minutes: 350` as a backstop, and
  a single model attempt may run for 45 minutes (the watchdog only gives up
  after 15 minutes without any output, because a long compile is silent but
  still working).
- **Auth** – the workflows read the token from the `OPENCODE_GITHUB_TOKEN`
  secret (an optional `PAT_TOKEN` secret wins) and may use the optional
  `OPENCODE_ADMIN_TOKEN` secret. No GitHub App has to be installed.
- **Agent install** – opencode is installed directly from the official installer
  (`curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/v2/install | bash -s -- --version 2.0.22`)
  instead of the `anomalyco/opencode` action, which used to fail on its version
  lookup step. The version is pinned on purpose.

## Fixing `Free usage limit reached`

When every model in the fallback chain stops with `Error: Free usage limit
reached` the GitHub Actions runner, the workflow and this repository are fine —
the limit is enforced on the OpenCode account server side. There is **no
permanent unlimited mode without either a subscription or a key**; the options,
in order of cost:

1. **Wait for the quota to reset.** The free models are rate limited per
   account; once the window passes the same workflow works again with no
   changes. (Current judged status: reset is not reliable.)
2. **Add free provider keys.** Create a free account at one or more of
   [Groq](https://console.groq.com/) (`GROQ_API_KEY`),
   [OpenRouter](https://openrouter.ai/) (`OPENROUTER_API_KEY`),
   [NVIDIA](https://build.nvidia.com) (`NVIDIA_API_KEY`),
   [Mistral](https://console.mistral.ai/) (`MISTRAL_API_KEY`) or
   [Cerebras](https://inference.cerebras.ai/) (`CEREBRAS_API_KEY`), then run
   `gh secret set <NAME> --repo mdmuntakim/opencode` for each. Set the repo
   variable `OPENCODE_MODELS` to a space separated fallback chain that lists
   those providers first, and the runner will use the free opencode models
   only as a last resort. Free tiers still rate limit, so this raises the
   ceiling; it does not remove it.
3. **Subscribe to OpenCode Go** ($10/month) or **Go Plus** — see
   [opencode.ai/v2/docs/console/go](https://opencode.ai/v2/docs/console/go/).
   Copy the key from the OpenCode Console and run
   `gh secret set OPENCODE_API_KEY --repo mdmuntakim/opencode`. Then set the
   `OPENCODE_MODELS` variable to e.g.
   `opencode-go/glm-5.3-flash opencode-go/kimi-k2.7-code opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash`
   (model ids from the Go docs). Paying is the only officially supported way
   to get sustained, reliable capacity.

The fallback wrapper treats quota/auth/stall failures from *any* model as a
signal to switch to the next one (it recognises `FreeUsageLimitError`,
`Free usage limit`, `429`, `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED`, `billing`, `quota`, `rate
limit`, `subscription`, `not configured`, `not authenticated`, `ProviderError`,
`model not found`, `model unavailable`, `401`/`403`, …), so an exhausted
provider, an unset key or a dead model no longer aborts the whole run before
the remaining models are tried.

### Logging the runner in instead of staying anonymous

GitHub-hosted runners share egress IPs, and anonymous free inference is
already saturated on them — the jobs fail with `Free usage limit reached`
even though the same models answer fine from a normal network connection.

Logging the runner into an OpenCode Console account lifts that anonymous
pool limit (`opencode auth login` → *Console* → *device*), and the token can
be handed to the workflow as a secret:

    opencode auth export > auth.json
    gh secret set OPENCODE_AUTH_JSON --repo mdmuntakim/opencode < auth.json

Both agent workflows import it with `opencode auth import` before the agent
starts, and stay anonymous when the secret is absent. The account still has to
satisfy its own free-tier limits; subscribing to OpenCode Go is the path to
sustained capacity.

## Secrets used

| Secret | Required | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `OPENCODE_GITHUB_TOKEN` | yes | Token used for the GitHub API and for git clone/fetch/push. Needs `repo` and `workflow` scopes to reach all repositories. With the `user` scope it can also change the profile, with `admin:public_key` it can manage the SSH keys. |
| `OPENCODE_ADMIN_TOKEN` | no | Fine grained token with `Administration: write`. It is the only way to create further tokens. |
| `OPENCODE_API_KEY` | no | Only needed if you switch away from the free model (e.g. an OpenCode Go key). |
| `OPENCODE_AUTH_JSON` | no | `opencode auth export` of an OpenCode Console login; when present the agent workflows authenticate instead of staying anonymous (fixes `Free usage limit reached` on GitHub-hosted runners). |
| `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, `GROQ_API_KEY`, `NVIDIA_API_KEY`, `MISTRAL_API_KEY`, `CEREBRAS_API_KEY` | no | Free-tier provider keys; together with the `OPENCODE_MODELS` repo variable they decide what the fallback chain tries. |

### Rotating the token

Create a classic personal access token with the `repo` and `workflow` scopes,
then update the secret:

```bash
gh secret set OPENCODE_GITHUB_TOKEN --repo mdmuntakim/opencode
```

### Adding the administration token

Create a **fine grained** personal access token for the `mdmuntakim` account with
the `Administration: write` permission, then store it:

```bash
gh secret set OPENCODE_ADMIN_TOKEN --repo mdmuntakim/opencode
```

With that secret the agent can create new personal access tokens through
`.github/scripts/gh-account.sh pat`.

# Nightly maintenance log

State carried from one autonomous run to the next. Each entry records what was
inspected, the single change that was made, how it was verified, and what is
still open, so the next run does not repeat the same investigation.

## 2026-10-28

**Area:** `.github/scripts/run-opencode-fallback.sh` (the runner both agent
workflows use).

**Finding:** every successful agent run in this repository ended as a failure.
After the model finished, the wrapper ran `npm test --if-present`; this control
repository has no `package.json`, and npm exits 254 in that case. The wrapper
interpreted that as "the agent broke the tests", re-ran the agent up to three
times with a bogus failure message, then returned 1 and failed the job. The
fallback chain was never reached because the log did not contain a provider
limit error.

Three smaller defects were found in the same path:

- `PROMPT` (the `workflow_dispatch` input and the value exported by
  `opencode-triage.yml`) was read by the workflow but never used by the script.
- Prompts were built with `"\n"` inside double quotes, so the agent received
  the two characters `\` and `n` instead of paragraph breaks.
- A stall or timeout killed `tee`, not the agent, and returned status 143
  instead of 124, so the next model was not tried and the agent kept running.

**Change:** gate post-run validation on a real `test` script in
`package.json`, use `PROMPT` first and build the prompt with `$'\n'`, run the
agent with its output redirected to the log and stream it with `tail -f`, kill
the actual process (TERM then KILL) and return 124 on stall/timeout. A failing
suite is fed back with the last 200 log lines. Added a stubbed-binary test
suite and a `scripts-test` workflow.

**Verification:** `shellcheck -x` is clean; the 19 assertions in
`.github/scripts/tests/run-opencode-fallback.test.sh` pass, including the
no-`package.json` success case, the failing-suite retry case and the stall
watchdog.

**Open, not changed this run:**

- The "Create or Update Pull Request Automatically" step in
  `opencode-triage.yml` runs against the checked out default branch and does
  not push the agent's branch. It is effectively dead today and its title uses
  an empty issue number on `workflow_dispatch`. It should be replaced by an
  explicit branch/push/PR step or removed by the owner.
- `publish-release.sh --help` prints only a slice of the header and the header
  contains a stray `#       --source-archive` line. Cosmetic.

### Second run, 2026-10-28

**Reported symptom:** the nightly run failed again with
`npm error path .../package.json` / `ENOENT`, and the retry prompt
("CRITICAL FIX REQUIRED") was passed back to the agent.

**Root cause:** the fix above exists only on the `test` branch. The
`opencode-triage` workflow checks out
`ref: ${{ github.event.repository.default_branch }}`, which is `main`, and
`main` still contains the old runner that calls `npm test` unconditionally.
Every issue-triggered run therefore executes the unfixed script from `main`;
the guard on `test` is never reached. This is a deployment gap, not a new
regression in the script.

**Change (on `test`):** resolve the manifest from `GITHUB_WORKSPACE` (the
checkout root, falling back to the current directory) and run `npm` from that
directory, so the guard and the invocation cannot disagree when a workflow
step starts in a subdirectory. Skip the gate when `npm` itself is missing.
Added two regression cases: a manifest without a `test` script must never
start `npm`, and a run from a subdirectory must validate the workspace root.
The suite is now 26 assertions.

**Verification:** `shellcheck -x` is clean; all 26 assertions pass.

**Open, needs the owner:** PR #93 (`test` → `main`) carries the runner fix and
must be merged before issue-triggered runs stop using the old script. Until it
is merged, no change on `test` can affect the workflow, because the workflow
always checks out the default branch. An alternative is to change the
checkout `ref` in `opencode-triage.yml` to the branch the agent uses.

### Third run, 2026-10-28

**Reported symptom (issue #92, still open):** every consumer of `npm test` at
the checkout root - the agent's post-run gate in this repository, and any
external harness - failed with

```
npm error path /home/runner/work/opencode/opencode/package.json
npm error enoent Could not read package.json
```

**Root cause:** the previous run fixed the guard inside the runner, but the
repository still had no manifest at all. Any `npm test` invocation that did
not go through the guard (the old runner on `main`, a CI harness, a developer)
hit ENOENT. Fixing the caller and leaving the missing file in place made the
failure dependent on which copy of the script ran.

**Change:**

- added `package.json` at the repository root: `npm test` runs
  `.github/scripts/tests/run-opencode-fallback.test.sh`, `npm run lint` runs
  `shellcheck`, `npm run check` runs both. The manifest is private, has no
  dependencies and adds no install step.
- `scripts-test.yml` now invokes `npm run lint` / `npm test`, so CI validates
  the same entry points the gate uses, and the workflow triggers on
  `package.json` changes.
- the runner test suite gained case 7: it asserts the repository manifest
  exists, parses as JSON and exposes a non-empty `test` script, and that the
  gate accepts it (31 assertions).

**Verification:** `npm test` (31 assertions) and `npm run lint` pass; the
runner still skips the gate for a manifest without a test script and for a
missing manifest.

**Still open:** the `issues` event always loads the workflow from the default
branch, so `main` must receive the runner and manifest through a pull request
(`test` → `main`) before issue-triggered runs use them. Nothing on `test` can
change what an issue-triggered run executes.

A new issue was opened on this repository. The issue title and body are appended below.

Please do the following:

1. Investigate. Read the files in this repository that are relevant to the issue.
   You also have a GitHub token with access to every repository of the owner, so you
   may read other repositories under `mdmuntakim/` if the issue relates to them

## Reply style

Write the answer as a normal chat message in Markdown. Do not paste raw JSON,
tool-call payloads, action logs, or internal transcripts into the issue or pull
request. Show a command and its human-readable result when it matters, but keep
the reply conversational and focused on the outcome.

Do not ask clarifying questions when the issue is understandable. If it is
ambiguous, state the assumptions you made and answer under those assumptions.
Keep the reply focused and skip pleasantries.
